PAGE.p: Experimental support for the SonicWall NetExtender SSL VPN protocol was added to OpenConnect in 2026. It was implemented from the behaviour of the official NetExtender 10.2 client for Linux.

NetExtender mode is requested by adding --protocol=netextender to the command line:
openconnect --protocol=netextender sslvpn.example.com

NetExtender logins take a domain as well as a username and password. It is LocalDomain by default, and a different one can be given with --authgroup:
openconnect --protocol=netextender --authgroup=CORP sslvpn.example.com

ul.li: One-time password (OTP) second factor, e.g. codes sent by email. This form has the ID _otp and the field name password, so the code can be given with --form-entry=_otp:password=123456. Software tokens (--token-mode) can generate the code too.

PAGE.p: Not yet supported: SAML/browser login, setting a new RSA SecurID PIN, changing an expired password, device registration (PDA), and End Point Control (EPC) checks.
The session cookie is called swap. Like other protocols, it can be obtained with --authenticate and passed to a later run with --cookie.

The tunnel carries PPP over TLS. Each PPP frame has a 4-byte big-endian length in front of it. The server picks either synchronous PPP (bare frames) or asynchronous PPP (an RFC1662 HDLC-like byte stream), and OpenConnect supports both. Older firmware that needs the legacy pppFrameEncoded=1 framing is not supported.

The client IPv4 address comes from PPP IPCP. Split routes, DNS servers and search domains come from the server's configuration response. When the server sets TunnelAllMode, a default route is used instead of split routes.
NetExtender does not use a UDP/DTLS transport.

This support was developed against the official client's behaviour and has not yet been tested against many real SonicWall appliances. If you can test it, please report results (good or bad) to the mailing list. Logs from -vvv --dump-http-traffic help us a lot, but check them for passwords and cookies before you send them.
